DEAD_EMPTY_STATE_FALSE_POSITIVE.reason: Guard clause null returns are intentional, not dead-end empty states requiring GovernedEmptyState
examples: if (!res.ok) return null; - server fetch failed, no data to render
if (!kpi.snapshots || kpi.snapshots.length < 2) return null; - insufficient data
if (!isOpen) return null; - conditional modal render
DEAD_EMPTY_STATE_FALSE_POSITIVE.scanner_issue: Cannot distinguish legitimate guard returns from dead-end empty states

RAW_ERROR_MESSAGE_INTERNAL.reason: Scanner flags all error.message usage. Runtime-errors.ts is internal error factory infrastructure, not user-facing error display
RAW_ERROR_MESSAGE_INTERNAL.scanner_issue: Cannot distinguish between internal error logging and user-facing error rendering
RAW_ERROR_MESSAGE_INTERNAL.action: NO_CODE_CHANGE - exempt internal infrastructure from governance:scan:strict

UNSAFE_ERROR_RENDER_INTERNAL.reason: RuntimeError class methods are infrastructure that CREATE operator-safe messages, not render them unsafely
UNSAFE_ERROR_RENDER_INTERNAL.context: These are error constructors and factories, not render methods
UNSAFE_ERROR_RENDER_INTERNAL.action: NO_CODE_CHANGE - exempt error factory from governance:scan:strict

UNSAFE_METRIC_FALSE_POSITIVE.reason: Scanner flags metric variable names in template strings (e.g., `${metric}: +5.2`). These are internal condition descriptions, not metric value rendering to operators
examples: condition: `${metric} returns to baseline or improves by >20%` - 'metric' is variable name like 'conversion_rate'
reason_parts.push(`${metric}: +${adj.toFixed(1)}`); - log message, not operator UI

TELEMETRY_SANITIZER_ACCEPTABLE.reason: Telemetry sanitizer is intentionally redacting error messages. This is CORRECT governance behavior, not a violation.
